objective: Map a dependency-light scoring/abstention/leakage architecture for F2-WP-803 that does not weaken its public-observation-only boundary or force probabilistic output where the public outcome space is not declared.

evidence_consumed.scope: public/evaluator-private boundary; prequential prediction-before-step ordering; selective risk plus coverage; held-out split identity; optional strictly proper probabilistic scoring
ObservationView is an explicit public whitelist; MicroWorldFixture/WorldNode retain evaluator-only hidden state; public_fixture_sha256 is distinct from full fixture identity

evidence_consumed.source: Gneiting and Raftery, Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
evidence_consumed.scope: strictly proper rules incentivize truthful probabilistic forecasts; Brier/quadratic and log score are canonical finite-outcome examples

evidence_consumed.source: Waghmare and Ziegel, Proper Scoring Rules for Estimation and Forecast Evaluation
evidence_consumed.scope: 2026 review confirming proper scoring rules as principled probabilistic forecast evaluation tools

evidence_consumed.source: Geifman and El-Yaniv, Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
evidence_consumed.scope: abstention is evaluated through a risk-coverage tradeoff rather than accuracy alone

evidence_consumed.source: Wang et al., Search-Time Contamination in Deep Research Agents
evidence_consumed.scope: evaluation leakage can inflate benchmark results; controlled access and transparent trajectories are recommended. Structural analogy only: WP803 is not a web-search benchmark.

architecture_findings.finding: UNKNOWN/abstain must remain outside ordinary correctness scoring.
architecture_findings.reason: A single accuracy number can reward an always-abstain policy or hide the cost of refusal. The benchmark should report at minimum eligible_count, predicted_count, abstained_count, coverage, conditional error/risk on predicted cases, and unconditional wrong-count/rate.

architecture_findings.finding: Do not make probabilistic forecasts mandatory in generation 1 unless the outcome vocabulary is independently public and predeclared.
architecture_findings.reason: A probability vector requires a public finite outcome space. Deriving candidate outcomes from evaluator-only nodes/transitions would itself leak holdout structure. Point prediction plus UNKNOWN is therefore the fail-closed default when no public outcome vocabulary exists.

architecture_findings.finding: When a public categorical outcome vocabulary does exist, add bounded Brier score as the preferred generation-1 proper score; keep log score optional/later.
architecture_findings.reason: Both are strictly proper, but Brier is dependency-free and bounded for finite categorical outcomes. Log score requires explicit zero-probability/clipping semantics and can become unbounded, adding avoidable benchmark-policy complexity.

architecture_findings.finding: Prediction must be identity-sealed before evaluator advancement; the realized next public ObservationView is the only scoring target.
architecture_findings.reason: This enforces a prequential boundary and blocks post-step rewriting. Prediction identity should bind episode_id/generation, fixture_id/generation, public_fixture_sha256, step_index, input ObservationView digest, policy/config digest, and prediction payload digest.

architecture_findings.finding: Baseline fitting and holdout evaluation identities must be separate.
architecture_findings.reason: Any empirical transition/frequency baseline fit on held-out fixture transitions contaminates the benchmark. A learned baseline must carry a fit_split_id/digest that is provably disjoint from holdout_set_id; otherwise use fixed public-information-only deterministic baselines.

architecture_findings.finding: Same-process Python can enforce a typed cooperative provenance boundary, not adversarial secrecy.
architecture_findings.reason: Passing only ObservationView through the benchmark API prevents accidental leakage, but hostile code in the same interpreter can still reach globals/closures/imports. WP803 generation 1 should claim repository/API leakage resistance only; hostile-plugin secrecy requires a future separate process/sandbox trust boundary.

required: Keep the current explicit ObservationView whitelist as the sole prediction input surface.
Represent point prediction as PREDICTED or UNKNOWN; do not coerce UNKNOWN into an ordinary outcome label.
Seal PredictionRecord before calling the canonical WP800 evaluator step and reject step/generation/input-digest mismatch.
Score against the subsequently materialized public ObservationView only.
Report coverage and selective risk/error together; add an always-UNKNOWN baseline/falsifier so abstention cannot masquerade as high accuracy.
Bind every learned/public-information baseline to an immutable fit-split/config digest and fail closed if it aliases the held-out family/split.

If probabilistic categorical prediction is supported, require an independently public outcome-vocabulary digest and compute Brier score; reject probability vectors whose labels originate from evaluator-private fixture enumeration.
falsifiers: ALWAYS_UNKNOWN must not win by accuracy-only reporting; coverage must become 0 and the report must expose it.

HIDDEN_STATE_SENTINEL: mutate evaluator-only hidden_ground_truth_ref/sha while keeping public ObservationView identical; prediction input digest and policy output must remain unchanged for a deterministic policy.
POST_STEP_REWRITE: attempt to construct/submit a prediction after evaluator advancement or with the next step_index; reject.
HOLDOUT_BASELINE_CONTAMINATION: baseline fit_split_id/digest equals or contains the held-out family/split; reject.
PRIVATE_OUTCOME_ENUMERATION: probabilistic vocabulary is derived from fixture.nodes/transitions instead of public config; reject.
SAME_PROCESS_THREAT_BOUNDARY: document that deliberate Python global/closure exfiltration is outside generation-1 secrecy credit rather than claiming cryptographic isolation.
metrics: exact_match_rate on all eligible cases with UNKNOWN counted separately, not silently dropped
optional mean Brier score only for genuine public-vocabulary probabilistic forecasts
baseline-relative deltas reported separately from absolute metrics

counterhypotheses.statement: The active WP803 implementation may already contain all of these fences, making this architecture delta redundant.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: Inspect the first WP803 source/test commit and run the listed adversarial unit tests. If all pass with equivalent metrics/provenance, adopt no additional architecture change.

counterhypotheses.statement: Mandatory probabilistic scoring would improve sensitivity enough to justify expanding generation-1 scope.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: Only promote it if a public outcome vocabulary exists without holdout leakage and an ablation shows added discrimination beyond point+UNKNOWN metrics at negligible complexity/latency.

counterhypotheses.statement: Same-process input whitelisting proves hidden-state secrecy.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: A deliberately hostile in-process predictor that imports/reaches evaluator state can bypass cooperative API boundaries; therefore no adversarial secrecy credit is granted at this scope.

handoff: TRIGGERWORD_4: consume this E2 delta while implementing F2-WP-803. Prefer point+UNKNOWN plus risk/coverage as mandatory generation-1 behavior; add Brier only behind an independently public outcome-vocabulary contract. Run exact hidden-sentinel, always-abstain, post-step, split-contamination and malformed-probability falsifiers before bounded repository-component acceptance.
